success_patterns: Answers matched the slot noun exactly: 'this Crimean city' gave Yalta rather than the conference, and 'this woman's gallery' gave the owner (Peggy Guggenheim) rather than the gallery name already in the clue.
When the clue named sub-kinds ('great horned & screech varieties of these birds'), the agent answered the parent category in plural (Owls), not a species named in the passages.
When the clue was a pun or parody name ('Rock group Achtung Babies'), the agent found that the passages call it a tribute band and answered the original artist (U2).

Verbatim clue phrases in the passages (the 'labor-intensive fruit' quote, the J! Archive line for Blaise Pascal) led straight to the answer. A trailing '(15)' letter count was used to confirm the candidate.
The answer was given as the bare core entity with no descriptors, which made exact match succeed (violet, Pascal, U2, Rumpelstiltskin).

patch.reasoning: Earlier epoch steps rejected broad structural edits such as a mandatory answer line, so only a few narrow, low-risk bullets are proposed. They cover two successful behaviours that existing rules only partly state: pun or tribute-act names resolving to the original artist, and clues that list sub-kinds resolving to the parent category. The third bullet adds a possessive-owner rule that restates the existing Peggy Guggenheim-style success in generic terms. None of them touches Rule 3 or the form rules that drive the stable passes.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - Pun, parody or tribute-act names ('Rock group Achtung Babies', a cover band or spoof title): the clue's name is only a play on the original. Check whether the passages describe it as a tribute or parody ('U2 tribute band'), and answer the ORIGINAL artist or work it riffs on (U2), not the pun name itself.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - Clue names sub-kinds of 'these <things>' ('the great horned & screech varieties of these birds', 'the Denver and Boston types'): the answer is the PARENT category that contains all of them, in the clue's number (plural for 'these'): 'Owls', not 'great horned owl'. Never answer with one of the named sub-kinds.

edits.content: - 'This woman's / man's <gallery, company, theory, ship>' with the thing already named in the clue: the answer is the OWNER, founder or creator (a person's full name), not the named thing. Pick the person whom most passages tie to the named thing ('Art of This Century' -> Peggy Guggenheim).
